entries.proposition: Ethosuximide abolished spontaneous spike-wave discharges in these mutant-model mice, while baclofen worsened them; the ethosuximide arm is within-animal before and after in four mice with no wild-type or vehicle arm described, since control mice do not have the discharges.
entries.snippet: Ethosuximide had an acute effect on the frequency of SWDs and abolished SWDs 30 min after treatment (Fig. 4C and E).
entries.anchor: Results, PV-ArchT mice displayed an absence seizure phenotype

entries.proposition: The measured T-type current is LOWER, not higher, in the model's reticular-nucleus PV neurons: peak T-current about 155 pA against about 699 pA in control and rebound bursts impaired, with three mice per group as the statistical unit.
entries.snippet: ArchT-expressing TRN PV cells possessed significantly lower peak current than controls (Fig. 6F) (155 ± 68 pA for PV-ArchT versus 699 ± 36 pA for controls, t4 = −7, P = 0.006: Fig. 6G).
entries.anchor: Results, ArchT expression impaired hyperpolarization-induced rebound excitation in TRN PV-positive neurons

entries.proposition: The authors write that these negative data indicate that alterations in Cav mRNA expression levels could not account for the ethosuximide-sensitive component of cortical and thalamic hyperactivity.
entries.snippet: These negative data indicate that alterations in Cav mRNA expression levels could not account for the ethosuximide-sensitive component of cortical and thalamic hyperactivity.
